nodes.label: JevRunner
nodes.rationale: One HTTPS request per lead carrying all four typed questions, with the connection reused across leads because a fresh TLS session costs about 600ms from this machine and has nothing to do with the model.

nodes.label: build_state() structured lead state
nodes.rationale: The lead record is passed as structured state rather than prose, which is the native input shape for a typed decision model.

nodes.label: JevRunner.measure_connect_cost() TLS handshake floor
nodes.rationale: Median wall time of a cold TCP+TLS handshake, reported alongside the results so the network floor is visible instead of being quietly folded into the model's latency number.

nodes.label: JevRunner.run()
nodes.rationale: Three attempts with connection teardown and backoff, because a reused keep-alive socket can drop; emits the same prediction/confidence/latency/cost record shape as ClaudeRunner so score.py needs no per-runner branches.

nodes.label: _intent_label() score-to-level mapping
nodes.rationale: Jev returns a continuous score plus a legend; the score is rounded and clamped to the nearest level, and the legend mapping is preferred over the raw index so a future reordering on the vendor's side cannot silently shift the mapping.

nodes.label: USD_PER_INPUT_TOKEN ($42 per billion, input only)
nodes.rationale: Output tokens are not billed at all, because the output is a label and a number rather than prose.

nodes.label: noul probability with a 0.5 decision threshold
nodes.rationale: A noul answer is a probability, not a boolean: 0.5 is applied as the decision threshold for the prediction while the raw probability is kept separately so calibration (Brier, ECE) can be scored without re-running the benchmark.
